title: Polyrhythm throughput sampler - annotated scratch
content:
Polyrhythm throughput sampler - notes (informal)

Goal:
- Explore mixed arrival workload: periodic pulse overlayed with Poisson noise (2:1 amplitude ratio). See if phase offsets cause synchronized KV-cache thrashing / tail amplification.

Hypothesis:
- When periodic pulse aligns with bursty Poisson clusters, pipeline stalls + cache miss cascades create transient p99 spikes independent of sustained QPS.

Environment:
- Model: rwd-7b-q4_0 (int8-ish) pinned v2026-01-21
- Serving: single dedicated pod (4xA10G), runtime branch: feature/polyrhythm-bench (PR 899)
- Instance: aws p4d-like equivalent, 64GB GPU mem reserved, 8 vCPU
- Client: bench-client v0.9 (gRPC + http fallback), 200 client threads from 3 hosts
- KV cache: enabled, capacity 16k entries, LRU, prefix caching on
- Batching: dynamic, max-batch 64, batch-timeout 6ms

Experiment matrix (short):
1) Baseline Poisson only (lambda = 300 qps)
2) Periodic only (pulse 1s period, 800 qps peak for 50ms)
3) Polyrhythm aligned (periodic pulse aligned to Poisson high-phase)
4) Polyrhythm anti-aligned (pulse shifted 250ms from Poisson peaks)
5) With prefix cache disabled (same as 3)
6) With batch timeout reduced to 2ms (same as 3)

Key commands (for reproducibility):
- bench-client run --pattern=poisson --lambda=300 --duration=600s --concurrency=120 --target=http://pod:8080/gen
- bench-client run --pattern=polyrhythm --pulse-qps=800 --pulse-width-ms=50 --lambda=300 --phase-offset-ms=0 --duration=600s

Selected raw results (median of 3 runs each):
- Baseline Poisson (300 qps): p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=78ms, qps=298, gpu_util=52%, cpu_idle=38%
- Periodic only (pulses): p50=21ms, p95=58ms, p99=130ms, qps=410 (avg), gpu_util=66%
- Polyrhythm aligned: p50=22ms, p95=76ms, p99=420ms (!), observed tail cluster around pulse windows, qps(avg)=360, gpu_util=71%
- Polyrhythm anti-aligned: p50=20ms, p95=49ms, p99=95ms, qps(avg)=370, gpu_util=60%
- Polyrhythm aligned + cache off: p50=27ms, p95=120ms, p99=990ms (severe), qps(avg)=340
- Polyrhythm aligned + batch-timeout=2ms: p50=19ms, p95=68ms, p99=310ms, qps(avg)=395

Quick observations:
- Alignment matters: when pulses align with natural Poisson clusters we see huge amplification of p99 (4-10x).
- KV cache substantially reduces severity; with cache off, p99 becomes multi-second and throughput drops. Strong sign of cache working as amortization for repeated prefixes in pulse windows.
- Reducing batch timeout recovers throughput and partial tail reduction — smaller batches reduce head-of-line blocking in the attention kernel path at the cost of GPU efficiency (util drops ~5-8%).
- GPU utilization correlates with throughput but not with p99 — high util plus p99 implies contention/serialize events not simple idle time.

Trace snippets (notes):
- 00:12:34 - spike window: many requests show identical prefix hash, KV-miss thrash events logged; GC-like CPU jitter on the host at same ms boundary.
- 00:18:02 - 2x cache-evictions logged inside 40ms; eviction policy thrashes with pulse.

ASCII throughput sweep (aligned run, aggregated):
[0s] ===        (120 qps)
[100s] ========  (260 qps, Poisson baseline)
[200s] ================= (peak pulses 800 qps) -> p99 spikes

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Is eviction window length (cache capacity & TTL) the dominant knob? Try increasing KV entries to 64k and repeat.
- Are batch formation heuristics exacerbating serialization? Instrument batch latency distribution and kernel queue lengths.
- Is client-side synchrony (many threads with same seed) amplifying alignment artificially — run with client jitter randomized at ms granularity.

Next steps / TODO:
- [ ] Run aligned/anti-aligned matrix with KV size 64k and 128k (Maya to help with infra).
- [ ] Add per-request prefix-hash sampling to telemetry and add dashboard heatmap (small Confluence doc: CONFLUENCE-3112).
- [ ] Try hybrid queue: allow small-priority lane that bypasses batching (quick wins seen when we bounded batch-size in earlier runs).
- [ ] Share results with SRE to diagnose host-level CPU jitter (Samir assigned).
- [ ] Add micro-tracing around batch formation + kernel dispatch (PR 899 is starting point).

Quick notes to self:
- When writing up, emphasize 'phase' rather than 'burst' — polyrhythm framing resonates with product folks.
- Avoid concluding that cache is silver bullet; it's necessary but not sufficient — pairing cache tweaks with batching heuristics yields best ROI.

End of scratchpad.

Jin
